description: Hydro-expansive, rubber-based hydrophilic sealant paste in tubes, applied using an extrusion gun
whereToUse: Mapeproof Swell has been specially developed to form flexible, waterproof seals in cracked reinforced concrete or in prefabricated elements with infiltration of water.
Sealing pipe-work which passes through concrete.
Sealing cold joints in reinforced concrete structures.
Sealing where water seeps through cracks in reinforced concrete structures.
Sealing lights and drainage outlets in swimming pools and tanks.
Sealing construction joints in concrete walls.
notFor: Do not apply Mapeproof Swell if the surface on which it is to be applied is highly contaminated with acid or solvents.
Do not use Mapeproof Swell on dirty or weak surfaces.
This product is not suitable for surface only application, and must always be confined.
The substrate may be damp, but there must be no water on the surface.

consumption.basis: Linear metres of bead per single cartridge, for a bead with a diameter of from 6 to 13 mm (APPLICATION PROCEDURE)
consumption.quote: With a single cartridge, approximately 3 metres of bead with a diameter of from 6 to 13 mm may be formed.
Each cartridge forms approximately 3 metres of Mapeproof Swell.

consumption.basis: Volume of product per linear metres of bead (technical data table)
consumption.quote: Consumption: approximately 320 ml per 3 linear metres

consumption.basis: Normal bead size (diameter of the extruded bead; not a consumption rate)
consumption.quote: The normal size of the bead is from 6 to 13 mm.

storage: Mapeproof Swell may be stored for up to 12 months in a dry place and at a temperature between +15°C and +25°C.
notes: The sheet gives one coverage figure only - approximately 3 metres per 320 ml cartridge - stated three times (application text, CONSUMPTION section, technical data table) and consistently. It is tied to a bead-diameter RANGE of 6 to 13 mm, not to one bead size, and no table of metres versus bead size is printed, so a calculator cannot vary yield by bead diameter from this sheet; use 3 m per cartridge. (My own arithmetic, not in the sheet: 320 ml over 3 m is a section of about 107 mm2, which matches the upper end of that range, so a thin 6 mm bead would not be limited to 3 m.) Temperature wording conflicts: TECHNICAL CHARACTERISTICS says the product 'may be used at any temperature', while the table prints 'Recommended application temperature range: from +5°C to +40°C'. The description says 'paste in tubes'; PACKAGING and the text say 320 ml cartridges. Other dimensions in the application text that are not consumption figures: cracks/joints broken out 'to a depth of at least 6 cm', and a confining boundary of 'at least 5 cm' when applied either side of a Lamposilex plug. Expansion is printed as 'Volumetric expansion in water: minimum 100%' and hydrostatic resistance as 'Sealing of water: 1 ATM'. No standards or classifications are stated (DIN/ISO references in the table are test methods, kept in the labels).
